To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the receptor potentials of the photoreceptor axons of transplanted eyes, which have no synaptic connections, are identical to those of normal eyes.
the photoreceptor membrane potential can be recorded in intact receptor cells that lack synaptic connections with the brain.

(a) the receptor potential of the photoreceptor cell can be recorded from the intact cell, (b) the receptor potential can be recorded from a photoreceptor cell that has no synapses with the central nervous sytem, and (c) a graded response is generated in the photoreceptor soma and axon without significant feedback control.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of the eye and the optic lobe of the fly.
the development of the visual system of the housefly.
the properties of the photoreceptor membrane in the absence of synapses and with the development of the photoreceptive system in flies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the receptor cells of the transplanted retinulae are functionally normal and indistinguishable from normal photoreceptors.
the photoreceptor cell is an independent unit, capable of generating a graded response to light without synaptic interaction.
the receptor potential of intact photoreceptors is a graded response to light, and that this response is independent of synaptic activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the photoreceptor is a simple, self-contained, electrogenic, sensory transducer.
the receptor potentials of the isolated cells are generated by the transduction mechanism of the photoreceptor cell and that the receptor potential is not influenced by the synapses.
the photoreceptor cell is a self-sufficient sensory organ.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the photoreceptor membrane is capable of producing a receptor potential without synaptic input, but that synaptic feedback is required to generate the normal spike responses.
, at least in the case of the fly photoreceptors, the development of the optic lobe does not appear to be necessary for the development of the photoreceptor cell.
the receptor potential is a fundamental property of the photoreceptor membrane, and that it does not depend on the presence of the synapses.
